diagnosis: Cutaneous Adverse Food Reaction (Chicken protein allergy).
treatment: Initiated 8-week novel protein elimination diet (hydrolyzed salmon). Prescribed short course of oral apoquel and soothing hypoallergenic foam baths.
followUp: Re-evaluate abdominal coat regrowth in 4 weeks.

symptoms: Hesitation climbing stairs in morning, slower gait after moderate park exercise.
treatment: Started monthly polysulfated glycosaminoglycan injections (Adequan) and daily glucosamine chews. Designed low-impact swimming exercise routine.

symptoms: Sudden vomiting after ingesting foreign table scraps, mild lethargy, normal hydration.
diagnosis: Acute Non-Obstructive Gastritis. Abdominal radiograph clear of foreign bodies.
treatment: Subcutaneous fluid therapy with B-complex, antiemetic injection (Cerenia), and 48-hour bland diet (boiled chicken breast and white rice).
followUp: Resolved within 48 hours. Regular diet resumed successfully.
